2.en: An Inquisitorial Rosette is a badge of holy office, wielded by Inquisitors and their agents to bypass the order of common, lesser souls and respected by all factions, institutes and houses of the Imperium. The construction and function of Rosettes are as varied as the Inquisitors who bear them, and carry the classified attributes of their masters’ power and duties. Some carry genetically encoded details of an Inquisitor’s identity and prove they operate with the Throne of Terra’s authority

12.en: Rosettes are rarely used in dealings with the common populace of Imperial worlds. To flaunt Inquisitorial authority is to draw attention, elicit fear, and demand absolute acquiescence. Rosettes see sparing use in ground-level investigations, for the sight of one will often sow word of the Inquisition’s presence, spreading unease through a local populace and alerting those who would prefer their heretical deeds remained in the shadow. In the rare moments when a Rosette is bared in this manner of investigation, it is understood by those who view it as a marker of absolute authority, and that a dreadful fate looms for those who fail to comply.

16.en: Some are made to the specifications of the Inquisitor bearing them, while many others existed long before their bearer’s birth, created by those they may never meet. A Rosette could be an inheritance or gift from a predecessor, a holy relic used for millennia assigned to an Inquisitor in recognition of their pious deeds, or an artwork of its own right commemorating victories long since wiped from Imperial records. The diversity of Rosettes also lies deeper than in aesthetics, with some featuring internal data probes and many incorporating gene locks to ensure that only the Inquisitor and those they deem worthy can handle the rosette, where tamperers instead set off alarms or internal defence systems.

20.en: Inquisitors rarely allow their acolytes to use their unique Rosette. Instead, they often provide their acolytes with an emblem, pendant, ring, or badge representing their authority or, in rare cases, a sanctioned simulacra of their Rosette. Most operatives bear this symbol discreetly as part of their clothing or uniform, easily hidden or revealed at a moment’s notice — thereby bearing a sliver of their Inquisitor’s terrible authority into the field.

24.en: Not all Rosettes have a special function beyond representing the Inquisitor’s authority. However, you can use the following tables to roll for or choose a unique effect and form that fits an Inquisitor character’s or Patron’s Rosette.
